title: Runtime orchestrator: SLA-aware soft-handoff router, kernel scoring, and commit-confidence metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a runtime-side orchestrator that performs a soft-handoff (tentative routing) between candidate model variants during prefill and decode. The orchestrator must pick kernels and attention execution modes per-candidate, compute a compact commit-confidence score for early outputs, and manage SLA-preserving fallbacks when confidence thresholds are not met or kernels are unavailable.
motivation: We need a low-latency mechanism to try faster model/quantization/kernel combos optimistically while providing deterministic safety nets so customer-facing SLOs (p50/p99 latency and error budget) are not violated. Current hard cutovers are costly: either always run the slow but accurate path or risk user-visible regressions. Soft-handoff + commit-confidence lets us get low-cost wins with controlled rollback.
scope: Implement orchestrator logic inside the serving runtime and add telemetry. Work includes: kernel-scoring function, attention-mode selector (block/fused/flash), commit-confidence metric design, inline fallback policy, lightweight state machine for soft-handoff, API flags for experiments, and e2e test harnesses. Does NOT include UI rollout controls (Console work will be a follow-up PM ticket).
out_of_scope: Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies, Console visualization, Private deployment packaging, model training/inference accuracy improvements at model-level.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can route a request to a tentative candidate and compute a commit-confidence score within 2ms (median) added overhead
End-to-end p99 latency for a representative text-gen workload does not increase by >5% when soft-handoff is enabled
Fallback path triggers and completes within configured SLA window when commit-confidence < threshold or kernel fails
Telemetry surfaces commit-confidence, kernel-choice, attention-mode, fallback-reason, and end-to-end latency in the runtime dashboard
Automated tests simulate kernel OOM and confirm graceful fallback without request loss
implementation_notes: Kernel scoring: compute a weighted score = alpha*estimated_throughput + beta*expected_memory_headroom + gamma*attention_fit_score; alpha/beta/gamma are config tunables per-customer-tier
Attention selector: detect pattern (dense-localized vs. global) from prefill token stats; prefer fused/flash kernels for global attention when supported, otherwise fall back to block-sparse kernels
Commit-confidence: a lightweight scalar [0..1] combining log-prob delta between tentative and canonical model on prefix, decode alignment metrics, and kernel-execution-success signals
Soft-handoff state machine: TRY -> EVALUATE (collect commit-confidence) -> COMMIT or RETRACT -> LOG and POSSIBLE FALLBACK
Fallback policy: immediate fallback if confidence < hard_threshold OR kernel error; otherwise allow up to N speculative tokens before rollforward depending on route_safety_profile
Config surface: per-route policy flags (speculative_enabled, soft_handoff_window, hard_threshold, max_spec_tokens, kernel_affinity_override)
tradeoffs: Higher spec window increases opportunity for cost savings but raises risk of user-visible incoherence if wrong candidate commits
More conservative kernel scoring (favoring stability) yields fewer performance wins but lowers fallback frequency
Complex commit-confidence models reduce false positives but add runtime overhead; we bias towards very cheap signals first and a tiered decisioning approach
decision_record: 2026-02-25: Use a scalar commit-confidence instead of full distribution to keep decision path fast (agreed by runtime and research)
2026-03-02: Kernel scoring will be implemented in two phases: Phase A (heuristic weights) for runtime rollout, Phase B (light ML model) if Phase A shows utility
2026-03-08: Default soft-handoff window set to 3 tokens for public rollout; can be increased in experimental buckets
testing_plan: Unit tests for kernel-scoring math and attention pattern detector
Integration tests that inject kernel failures (OOM, timeout) and assert fallback within SLA window
Load test with synthetic mix: 60% short prompts, 30% medium, 10% long to measure p50/p95/p99 latency changes
A/B experiment in staging region with traffic mirroring to validate quality regressions under a held-out prompt set
Fuzz tests around commit-confidence thresholds to ensure no infinite RETRACT loops
rollout_plan: Canary: 1% traffic in staging cluster with spec_enabled=true and detailed telemetry
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 75% over 3 days with monitoring gates on p99 latency and fallback rate
Kill-switch: route flag to instantly disable soft-handoff per region and per-route
Postmortem: auto-capture last 100 routed requests when a rollback gate trips for debugging
metrics: speculative_success_rate = fraction of tentative routes that commit without fallback
observability_notes: Instrument commit_confidence and kernel_choice as top-level dimensions in runtime traces. Add tags for attention_mode, route_policy, and spec_bucket. Dashboard should provide correlation views between commit_confidence and post-commit token perplexity (sampled).
operational_risks: Increased telemetry volume (commit_confidence per request) — mitigate by sampling low-priority customers
Edge-case kernels that report success but produce corrupted KV cache — add checksum + quick-verify pass before commit
SLO thrash if fallback storms occur during infra blips — implement exponential backoff on re-trying speculative candidates
